title.narrative: Core support Centre for Policies and Reforms 2022-2025
Kärnstöd Centre for Policies and Reforms 2022-2025

description.narrative: Centre for Policies and Reform (CPR) grundades och registrerades som en moldavisk offentlig förening 2017. Dess uppgift är att främja demokrati, mänskliga rättigheter och reformer av god samhällsstyrning. bekämpa korruption; och underlätta Moldaviens europeiska integration. Den ursprungliga avsikten med organisationens grundande var att skapa en tankesmedja för att utveckla politiska förslag till regeringen. CPR har sedan dess tagit mer av en övervakande roll och utökat sina arbetsområden. CPR:s uppdrag är att främja tillgång till information och allmänhetens deltagande. ett ärligt och ansvarsfullt företagande; mänskliga rättigheter med fokus på mötes- och yttrandefrihet samt tillgänglighet och insyn i rättsväsendet. CPR arbetar på lagstiftningsnivå och föreslår politik och förordningar; bygger upp kapaciteten hos offentliga tjänstemän och institutioner och engagerar medborgarna och utrustar dem med nödvändiga demokratiska färdigheter för att delta i beslutsprocessen. CPR försvarar rättsstatsprincipen, demokratins värden och mänskliga rättigheter. De övervakar, föreslår lösningar och uppmuntrar allmänhetens deltagande. CPR arbetar mot sin vision: ett samhälle fritt från korruption, med en demokratisk och ansvarstagande styrning och engagerade medborgare. Kärnstödet är att bidra till genomförandet av den organisatoriska strategin och resultatbedömningsramen som följer 5 mål: 1. CPR är en hållbar och professionell organisation som medborgarna litar på och respekterar av regeringen.2. Information av allmänt intresse är mer tillgänglig.3. Ett hälsosammare företagsklimat. 4. Medborgarna har större möjlighet att utöva yttrande- och mötesfrihet. 5. Ett öppnare rättssystem.

The Centre for Policies and Reform (CPR) was founded and registered as a Moldovan public association in 2017. Its mission is to advance democracy, human rights, and good governance reforms; fight corruption; and facilitate Moldova’s European integration. The original intention of the founders of the organisation was to create a think-tank for developing policy proposals to the government. CPR has since taken more of a watchdog role and expanded its areas of work.CPR’s mission is to promote access to information and public participation; an honest and responsible business; human rights with a focus on freedom of assembly and of speech and accessibility and transparency of the judiciary. CPR works at the legislative level, proposing policies and regulations; builds capacities of public servants and institutions and engages with citizens, equipping them with necessary democratic skills to get involved in the decision making process.CPR defends the rule of law, the values of democracy and human rights. They monitor, propose solutions and encourage public participation.CPR works towards their vision: a society free of corruption, with a democratic and accountable governance and involved citizens.The core support is to contribute to the implementation of the organizational stratgy and the Results Assessment Framework that follows 5 objectives:1. CPR is a sustainable and professional organisation trusted by citizens and respected by the government.2. Information of public interest is more accessible.3. A healthier business environment. 4. Citizens are more empowered to exercise freedom of speech and assembly.5. A more transparent justice system.

Strategic objective 1: CPR is a sustainable and professional organisation trusted by citizens and respected by the government.
Strategic objective 2: Information of public interest is more accessible.
Strategic objective 3: A healthier business environment.
Strategic objective 4: Citizens are more empowered to exercise freedom of speech and assembly.
Strategic objective 5: A more transparent justice system.

The project started in December 2022 and until the handover of the project no major issues were identified. The project team was consolidated and activities performed according to the action plan and strategic objectives. -- In the reporting period CPR managed to strengthen its role as a leading organization in the area of access to information and public participation by achieving results in all of its three areas of intervention: At the level of national policy, not only did CPR provide expert contribution and solutions to ongoing reform efforts in the area of access to information and public participation, but also acted as a facilitator for other civil society organizations, making these contributions more diverse and representative. At the level of capacities of public authorities, CPR successfully developed methodologies, tools and training programs to facilitate capacity building for both central and public authorities in the areas of transparency and public participation. It also piloted these instruments to the end of increasing transparency and public participation in selected national and local-level authorities. At the level of engagement of citizens in decision-making processes and using transparency and public participation tools to solve community issues, CPR completed the third edition of the Instigation to Democracy programme, by which it engaged over 50 beginner activists in using democracy tools to achieve social change. All of the above were complemented by communication products articles, guidelines and explainer materials, that ensure dissemination of know-how and encourage public debates on the topics of access to information and public participation.
2024 In 2024, CPR continued to engage with its governing structures, by holding one meeting of the Board and one of its General Assembly. The organization has continually engaged with its members and alumni.
In relation to Organizational Development, the team was expanded and internal decision-making and responsibilities were clarified. Still, in the Plans for 2025, it were included refining internal policies, building staff capacity, and securing diverse funding sources.
Referring to Access to Information, Transparency & Public Participation, the organization led national dialogue on improving access to information laws. The team provided training to 100 public servants; more outreach planned for 2025 including collaboration with ministries and recruitment from City Halls. CPR produced studies and articles to improve legal frameworks and citizen engagement. CPR co-organized Moldovas first Civic Engagement Conference, and continued to focus on legislation reform and citizen participation in decision-making. The "Instigation to Democracy" Project was at its fourth edition and involved women-led community initiatives, focusing on advocacy and civic involvement.
The team continued to rise their capacities and develop the Green Transition pillar. They monitored environmental legislation, trained researchers in policy writing.
In relation to Human Rights & Civil Liberties, CPR continued legal and policy work on refugee protections, monitored public assemblies. It will release findings and advocate for civil liberties especially during upcoming elections. During reporting period, the organization continued their strong commitment to gender sensitivity and inclusivity.
